base_member_text: the plotted eta is eta[0,:] (first row, L46), implying the loaded eta_ files are 2-D with the 1-D profile in row 0; file layout is not documented here
audit_member_text: np.loadtxt returns a 1-D array for a single-row eta file, but L46 unconditionally indexes eta[0,:], which fails for that common shape; there is no shape normalization/check.

base_member_text: the slope condition compares the integer index i to the position Xslp in meters (if i < Xslp, L22) — equivalent to comparing x[i] only because dx=1.0 (L12); would misplace the toe for other dx
audit_member_text: The slope condition compares array index `i` to physical coordinate Xslp at L22, while the actual coordinate is x[i]=i*dx at L18. It only locates the toe correctly because dx currently equals 1; changing dx moves the physical toe to Xslp*dx rather than Xslp.

base_member_text: dep is allocated as a full m x m array (L19) though only column 0 is read/written (L23, L25, L46) — mirrors the MATLAB zeros(m) square-matrix quirk of plot_solitary.m at the cost of an unnecessary 1024x1024 array
audit_member_text: A 1-D bathymetry is stored as an m-by-m matrix at L19 even though only column 0 is written/read (L23-L27,L46), consuming quadratic memory and leaving 1023 unused constant-depth columns. The MATLAB version's analogous square allocation caused multi-series plotting; this port avoids that only by explicitly selecting DEP[:,0].
